takeaway: Medial plantar nerve: flexor digitorum brevis, abductor hallucis, flexor hallucis brevis. Flexor digiti minimi brevis is supplied by the lateral plantar nerve.

question.text: Which of the following muscles in the sole of the foot is not supplied by the medial plantar nerve?

lines.text: The sole of the foot has four muscle layers, just like a layered cake.
The yellow waiter is the medial plantar nerve.
He serves flexor digitorum brevis, abductor hallucis, and flexor hallucis brevis.
The purple waiter is the lateral plantar nerve. It supplies abductor digiti minimi, quadratus plantae, adductor hallucis and the interossei.
And flexor digiti minimi brevis, the happy muscle on the right, is also lateral plantar.
So it is not supplied by the medial plantar nerve.
